root_cause.text: The `smb2_ioctl_query_info()` function in the SMB client subsystem fails to validate that the server-reported `OutputBufferLength` (which determines the copy size of the `qi_rsp->Buffer` flexible array) fits within the actual response buffer size (`rsp_iov[1].iov_len`), allowing an out-of-bounds read when copying data to userspace.
root_cause.evidence: The patch introduces a bounds check in `fs/smb/client/smb2ops.c` that verifies if `struct_size(qi_rsp, Buffer, qi.input_buffer_length) > rsp_iov[1].iov_len` and returns `-EFAULT` if the check fails, preventing `copy_to_user()` from reading past the response buffer.

intent_record.what: Added a conditional check to verify that the response buffer is large enough to accommodate the `qi_rsp` structure with the given `qi.input_buffer_length` using `struct_size`.
intent_record.how: Prevents potential out-of-bounds memory access by returning `-EFAULT` if the calculated structure size exceeds the actual response buffer length.
